title: Non-blocking findings from frontend-backend-feature-gap-audit's PR review (#400)
description: pr-reviewer's independent re-verification of PR #400 (frontend-backend-feature-gap-audit) confirmed the audit's three filed gaps (frontend-cftc-cot-display, frontend-trade-strategy-tagging, frontend-daily-homework-history) and its `divergence.aborted` override are all correct, and the task board validates cleanly. Two non-blocking findings surfaced during that independent re-check that the PR's own review process should not let disappear once PR #400 merges.

checklist.step: The audit's `decisions` entry on frontend-backend-feature-gap-audit.json cites `git log -S"abortedClause" ` as `commit 5018850f (PR #151-era)` to support that the divergence.aborted tooltip wiring predates the audit. The commit hash and date are correct, but the actual PR is #158, not '#151-era' (`git log --oneline` for 5018850f shows '(#158)'). Doesn't affect the conclusion (the wiring genuinely predates the audit either way), but the citation itself is wrong and should be corrected if that decisions entry is ever revisited.

An independent re-grep of every response-schema field (not just the ones the audit's own decisions entry listed) found 4 additional fields with zero production-component usage that the audit's exhaustive-sounding 'every other field checked... confirmed to have at least one real production consumer' claim missed entirely -- not listed in either its genuine-gap bucket or its deliberately-ruled-out-minor bucket: (1) `DivergenceOut.centerline_crossed` -- `metricHelpContent.ts`'s `divergenceHelp.interpretValue` branches on `divergence.indicator === 'macd_histogram'` instead of reading this field directly, even though the field's own docstring says it's always true exactly when indicator is 'macd_histogram' -- so the information is surfaced, just not by reading this exact field; (2) `InsiderTransactionOut.ownership` (yfinance's raw direct/indirect flag) -- `InsiderTransactionsPanel.tsx`'s table columns are date/insider/position/shares/value/transaction_text, no ownership column; (3) `YesterdayTradingSuggestionOut.as_of_date` and (4) `net_realized_pnl` -- `DailyHomeworkForm.tsx` reads `suggested_score` from this response but never surfaces the dollar amount or date behind it, so a user sees a prefilled 0/1/2 score with no visible reasoning. All four are judged minor/cosmetic -- the same class of finding the audit itself correctly bucketed elsewhere (SupportResistanceZone secondary metadata, IBKRBreadthSnapshotResponse.snapshot_date) -- not warranting their own feature task, but worth a UI-polish pass if someone is already touching these components: showing `net_realized_pnl` as supporting context for the suggested yesterday-trading score is the most plausibly worthwhile of the four.
